narration: You just got a two-dollar raise. Your boss is proud. Your coworkers are jealous. And you're about to quietly lose twelve thousand dollars.
visual: Person silhouette receives paycheck with '+$2/HR' glowing in amber. Then red warning signs and dollar bills flying away animate in.

narration: Here's why. If you earn below a certain amount, the government helps with groceries, healthcare, childcare, and rent. Together that's worth over thirteen thousand dollars a year.
visual: Four benefit cards spring onto screen: SNAP $6,000 | Medicaid $3,200 | Childcare $7,200 | Housing $3,400. Total banner: $19,800/year.

narration: But cross one specific income line — even by a single dollar — and all of it disappears overnight. That's called the benefits cliff. And it hits like a wall.
visual: Animated cliff chart: income bar grows left to right, then at a threshold line the net income bar sharply drops off a cliff edge.

narration: Do the math. A two-dollar raise on forty hours a week adds about four thousand dollars a year. But you just lost thirteen thousand in benefits. You're down nine grand.
visual: Animated equation: +$4,000 (raise) minus $13,000 (benefits lost) equals a big red -$9,000 counter that ticks down.

narration: This isn't rare. It traps thirteen million American households. People turn down overtime, refuse promotions, and stay stuck. They're not lazy — they're doing the actual math.
visual: Grid of 13 person silhouettes. Several have red X marks over upward arrows labeled 'PROMOTION' and 'OVERTIME'.

narration: Before you say yes to your next raise, check your income against benefit thresholds at benefits dot gov. That two-dollar bump might literally cost you more than it pays.
visual: Phone shape with screen showing a simple threshold meter and 'benefits.gov' label. Checkmark animation and 'KNOW YOUR CLIFF' headline.
